transformeRs wishlist

Source: WISHLIST.md

This is the working to-do list for the package’s palettes. It is deliberately a plain Markdown file so that adding a character is a one-line edit: put the character or team under Queued, and the next maintenance pass (a person, or a Claude Code session in this repo asked to “work through the wishlist”) turns each queued line into registry entries, tests, figures and docs. CLAUDE.md describes that procedure step by step.

Public requests arrive as GitHub issues from the request form; triage them into this file rather than working straight from the issue, so the queue and its priorities live in one place.

How to write a queued line

- [ ] **Name or team** (faction; team/subgroup; year) - priority: high | normal | low
      TFWiki: https://tfwiki.net/wiki/Name_(G1)
      Notes: members if a team, which colours matter, anything odd.

Only the bold name and a priority are required. When a line is done, move it to Done with the version it landed in. Keep the sections in this order; scripts and people both read from the top.

Conventions the entry must follow

  • One palette per character; combiner teams also get a palette for the combined form, listed last within the team. Team order is torso first, then limbs, then the combined form (tests enforce this).
  • Palette name: character name in lowercase snake_case (hun_gurrr, blast_off). Combined forms use their own name with no team prefix.
  • Colours: 4 to 6 hex values from the original Hasbro release, body plastic first, then secondary plastic, then chrome/die-cast/paint accents, most distinct first. Members of one team share hex values for shared plastics.
  • Metadata: character, faction, team, combiner, role (leader, combiner torso, combiner limb, combined form, or a new role if the subgroup needs one), alt_mode, year, description, TFWiki page, and a TFWiki toy photo URL where one exists (NA otherwise; the browser copes).
  • After adding: devtools::document(), devtools::test(), source("data-raw/make_figures.R"), update the Coverage table in README.md and the entry in NEWS.md, and rebuild the pkgdown site.
